_readme: Fill this file in and the page is done — nothing in index.html or scripts/ should need editing. Anything set to null disappears from the page. Run `node scripts/validate-config.js` when you are finished. See SETUP.md.

page.title: Regional parliament election in Berlin · 2026
page._postUrlComment: The WordPress post this page is embedded in. Used by scripts/check-embed.js, which is the only thing that looks at it — the page never calls back to the post. Set it once the post exists.
page._pagesUrlComment: Where this page is published. Publish it alongside the article: it is served from a CDN and executes no PHP, so it stays up when the WordPress host does not.
page.citation: Europe Elects. (2026, September 19). Germany: Regional parliament election in Berlin 2026. Europe Elects.
page.sources: Infratest dimap (ARD/rbb), Forschungsgruppe Wahlen (ZDF), INSA, Forsa, Landeswahlleiterin Berlin.

election.title: Regional parliament election in Berlin

jurisdiction._comment: `territory` is the sub-national unit for a regional election. Berlin is both a city and a Land, and elects a single chamber for both roles.

election._firstProjectionComment: ARD/rbb and ZDF publish an exit-poll Prognose the moment polls close at 18:00 and the first full Hochrechnung about a quarter of an hour later.
election._seatsFixedComment: false: the Abgeordnetenhaus has 130 statutory seats but overhang and levelling seats float the total upward — it sat at 159 after 2023. That lifts the ceiling on a seat projection rather than dropping the check.
election._seatsTotalComment: Statutory size: 78 constituency seats plus 52 list seats, 66 of 130 for a majority. Used to sanity-check seat figures coming out of the Sheet, with seatsFixed false widening the band.
election._thresholdComment: 5% of valid second votes, with an exemption for a party that wins a constituency seat outright — which is how a party polling below the threshold can still take seats.
election._ballotNameComment: Voters cast an Erststimme for a constituency candidate and a Zweitstimme for a party list. The Zweitstimme decides the seat distribution and is what this page reports.

previous.note: A repeat election ordered after the Constitutional Court annulled the 2021 vote; 159 seats including overhang and levelling seats
previous._comment: The election this one is compared against. The 26 September 2021 election was declared invalid in November 2022 over ballot shortages and misdelivered papers, and rerun in full on 12 February 2023 — so the outgoing parliament sat for three and a half years, not five.

sheet._idComment: A separate Sheet from the Mecklenburg-Vorpommern one on purpose: shared tab names would collide, and an analyst typing Berlin figures would trigger a Mecklenburg-Vorpommern rebuild. Must be shared as Anyone with the link → Viewer. Both the Action and the browser read this through the gviz CSV endpoint with no credentials at all, so a restricted Sheet returns HTTP 401 to everything — the pipeline, the page's fallback read, and Datawrapper's linked dataset alike.
sheet._tabsComment: Tabs are referenced by NAME, never by gid. A gid is regenerated every time a Sheet is duplicated; the name survives. These names are the ones that carry over from the Saxony-Anhalt Sheet — check them against the tab strip after copying.

results._comment: Layout of the `results` tab. Column 0 is always the party name; these are the 0-based indexes of the rest.
results._totalRowComment: Case-insensitive regular expression matching the label of the totals row, so it is summed as an electorate figure rather than mistaken for a party. Both spellings, because the Sheet is worked on in two languages.
results._votesAreComment: "count" is a raw vote count, and a percent sign in it then means the cell holds a placeholder rather than a figure — those rows read as not yet counted.
results._minValidVotesComment: Floor on the totals row. About 2.5 million people are eligible and 1,529,558 voted in 2023, so a real count clears 100,000 within the first reporting Bezirke. Below it the whole tab reads as not yet counting, so a half-prepared sheet cannot put placeholder figures on the page as results.

sheet._ignoredTabsComment: Tabs the Apps Script should NOT treat as a reason to rebuild — static reference data and the team's shift roster. Keep this in step with IGNORED_TABS in Script Properties. Deliberately a deny-list: forgetting to list a tab costs one wasted no-op run, whereas an allow-list fails silently and loses data. Note that _coa_exit_ID and _coa_exit_FGW are NOT here — analysts type into them live.

source._localPathComment: Path to a local PartiesData checkout, e.g. "../PartiesData". When set it is read instead of GitHub, which is how this runs offline and without a token. Left null because the Action has no checkout to read.
source._authComment: PartiesData is a private repository, so the build reads it through the GitHub Contents API with a token from PARTIESDATA_TOKEN (a fine-grained PAT with Contents: Read on it). In the Action that is a repository secret of the same name. See SETUP.md.
source._comment: This entry is Berlin's own, filed under Germany as an election type, and its last_results are the 12 February 2023 repeat election — so it is a real baseline and nothing has to be borrowed. Run `node scripts/fetch-parties.js --list` to print what exists for a country.

parties._metadataFallbackComment: Only group, colour and full name are taken from a fallback; last_results never is, because a federal result is not a state baseline. It is here so a federal spelling appearing in the Sheet (CDU/CSU, say) still resolves.
parties._baselineSourceComment: The PartiesData entry named above is this territory's own last election, so last_results is the correct previous-result column. content/previous-result.json carries the same figures with seats, for the accordion.
parties._orderComment: Ballot order of the 17 admitted lists, followed by dieBasis, which contested 2023 and is not standing again, so it sorts to the bottom of the results table.

overrides._comment: Keyed by the party's key in PartiesData. Every field is optional — anything omitted is derived. `aliases` adds spellings the Sheet may use; the key, the code and the display name already match automatically.

Tierschutz.name: Tierschutzpartei
Tierschutz._colorComment: Deliberate departure: PartiesData files this party under LEFT, which would give it Die Linke's dark red. The animal-rights palette entry is both truer and legible next to it. It took 2.4% in 2023, the strongest of the non-parliamentary lists.

PARTEI.name: Die PARTEI
PARTEI.full: Partei für Arbeit, Rechtsstaat, Tierschutz, Elitenförderung und basisdemokratische Initiative

Volt.name: Volt
Volt._colorComment: Volt's own brand purple, which is also the palette's Eurofederalist entry. Keeps it off the Greens' green.

Basis.name: dieBasis
Basis._comment: Contested 2023 (0.5%) and is not on the 2026 ballot. Kept so its 2023 figure has a name and a colour.

extra._comment: The seven smaller lists admitted for 2026 that the Berlin PartiesData entry does not carry, because none of them has a 2023 result recorded. `name` and `color` are required here — there is nothing upstream to derive them from. Worth adding to PartiesData proper rather than leaving here.

ÖDP.name: ÖDP
ÖDP._colorComment: Deliberate departure: its MEP sits with Greens/EFA, which would hand it the same green as Bündnis 90/Die Grünen.

SGP.name: SGP
SGP._colorComment: A lighter red than the DKP's, so the two communist lists are not one bar.

PdF.name: PdF
PdF._colorComment: PartiesData files PdF under RE elsewhere, which collides with the FDP's yellow.

sections._comment: The page is built from these, in this order. Set any section to null to remove it completely. Charts are Datawrapper embeds: `id` is the 5-character chart ID, `version` the published version in the embed URL (a fresh copy starts at 1), `live: true` means the chart reads the Sheet and the Action republishes it on every update.

results.label: Results
results.heading: All contesting parties
results.sub: The 17 lists admitted for 20 September 2026, with their European party affiliation, followed by dieBasis, which contested 2023 and is not standing again. Official second-vote results and the change vs. 2023 populate after polls close at 18:00 CEST.

projections.label: Projections
projections.heading: Infratest dimap & Forschungsgruppe Wahlen · projections over time
projections.sub: A mix of exit poll and counted result, published and revised by both institutes through election night
projections.note: Both institutes publish a first projection at about 18:15 CEST on 20 September 2026 and revise it as counting proceeds. These charts stay empty until then.

exitVotes.label: Exit Poll · Popular Vote
exitVotes.heading: Berlin 2026 · exit poll, popular vote
exitVotes.sub: Second-vote share by party, as published at 18:00 CEST when polls close
exitVotes.empty: Exit poll figures will appear here once published.

exitSeats.label: Exit Poll · Seats
exitSeats.heading: Berlin 2026 · exit poll, seat estimate
exitSeats.sub: Projected seats by party, as published at 18:00 CEST
exitSeats.empty: Exit poll seat estimates will appear here once published.

turnout.label: Turnout by the Hour
turnout.heading: Berlin 2026 · turnout by the hour
turnout.sub: Cumulative turnout reported through election day, local time
turnout.note: How turnout built through the day, this election against previous ones. Turnout was 62.9% at the February 2023 repeat election, well below the annulled 2021 vote, which was held alongside the federal election.

previousResult.label: 2023 Result · Outgoing Abgeordnetenhaus
previousResult.heading: Berlin 2023 · final result of the repeat election
previousResult.sub: 12 February 2023 · turnout 62.9% · 159 seats including overhang and levelling seats

polling.label: Pre-Election Polling
polling.heading: Voting intention since the 2023 repeat election
polling.sub: Polls published between the two elections · second vote (Zweitstimme)
polling._yMaxComment: Top of the y-axis, in percent. Fixed just above the CDU's 28.2% in 2023, since nothing has polled higher since.

sections._pollingHistoryComment: The long 1990-onward archive lives in the Sheet's `_pre-elex-polls` tab and has not been transcribed into content/poll-history.json yet. Set this section back to the shape in the template once it has.
sections._headToHeadComment: No published Direktwahlfrage series for the governing-mayor question was found. Turn this section on with content/head-to-head.json once one exists — Berlin does not elect its governing mayor directly, so it is a hypothetical question, and the CDU is standing Stefan Evers rather than the incumbent Kai Wegner.

coalitions.label: Coalition Options
coalitions.heading: Possible coalition combinations
coalitions.sub: Combined seat share of viable coalitions, per the latest Infratest dimap and Forschungsgruppe Wahlen exit poll
coalitions.note: Coalition arithmetic appears once the first exit poll is published at 18:00 CEST on 20 September 2026. 66 of 130 seats are a majority, more where overhang and levelling seats enlarge the chamber — and with four parties polling between 12% and 23%, no two-party combination is clearly available.

demographics.label: Demographic Vote
demographics.heading: Vote share by group, election over election
demographics.sub: Second vote (Zweitstimme) · Infratest dimap exit polls for ARD
demographics._panelsComment: How many independently-selectable charts to show side by side.
demographics._defaultCategoriesComment: One category name per panel, matching the Group column in the Sheet tab. These are the Saxony-Anhalt tab's spellings and carry over on a copy — correct them if the Berlin tab differs.
demographics._labelsComment: Optional display name and footnote per category, keyed by the Group value in the Sheet.
demographics._sourceComment: No seed: there is no transcribed Berlin demographic series yet, so the charts stay empty until the pipeline reads the Sheet tab once. Drop the result into content/demographic-seed.json and point this back at it if a first load should never be blank.

history.label: Electoral History
history.heading: Berlin · second-vote share and seats by election, 1990–2026
history.sub: First all-Berlin election after reunification onward · the 2026 column is not a certified result until counting finishes

sections._recordsComment: Off for now. The obvious block is Die Linke's strongest Berlin results — it has polled between 18% and 23% since mid-2026, against 12.2% in 2023 — but the comparator series was not sourced in time, and a ranked list of certified results is not worth publishing unchecked. Switch it on with content/records.json; the template has the shape.

automation._githubRepoComment: Used by scripts/ for log lines and by SETUP.md. The Action itself uses $GITHUB_REPOSITORY and the Apps Script reads its own GITHUB_REPO script property, so a wrong value here breaks nothing.

datawrapper._republishComment: Off. A published Datawrapper chart with a linked dataset fetches it in the reader's browser, so republishing does nothing for freshness — it mints a new version, which strands the version this config pins, and spends API quota shared across the organisation.

automation._republishUntilComment: Republishing stops this many days after election day, so a finished page cannot keep spending API quota forever.
automation._sheetFallbackComment: The page reads the generated JSON first and only falls back to reading the Sheet directly every Nth cycle — the Sheet sends no-store, so every reader hitting it goes to Google unbuffered.
